summary: Round 6's major is genuinely fixed in backlog.md:123 and the SPEC.md T0 mutation column now names the bare-pair mutation and its direction. The minting-site clause is right: IngestCommitPathTest's Recording sequencer is the correct fixture and both halves of the stated assertion are writable today. But this round's NARROWING of the delta payload from the triple to (incarnationId, flushSeq) was applied to backlog.md:123 and ADR line 97 and NOT to the two sentences that tell a session what to assert. backlog-notes.md:250 still prescribes 'the triple PER SegmentCommit' -- the shape the ADR rejects three lines later -- and both notes:254 and ADR:111 still say 'give those fixtures DIFFERENT triples per segment'. Measured against the three fixtures they name: all three differentiate their segments ONLY by pod, which is precisely the field the narrowing removed from the payload, so following that instruction literally leaves the once-per-delta mutation ALIVE in every one of them. One major, three minors. Every other test claim in the staged bytes was checked against the tree and holds.

findings.title: The notes still prescribe the TRIPLE per SegmentCommit, and the discriminator instruction that follows it now leaves the once-per-delta mutation alive in all three named fixtures
findings.detail:
backlog-notes.md:250 reads '`CommitDelta` carries the triple PER `SegmentCommit`, not once per delta.' in the section that opens 'It prescribes one now'. backlog.md:123 and ADR-0036:97-101 prescribe the PAIR and explicitly reject podId ('would put two independent pod attributions on one record with nothing forcing them to agree'). The layer-3 document a session reads for this row therefore prescribes the field the ADR in the same commit rejects. This is the fix-one-copy-miss-the-duplicate failure baselines/review.txt already records for M4.10a and M4.10.

THE SURVIVING MUTATION, which is the part in my lane. notes:254 and ADR:111 both say 'Give those fixtures DIFFERENT triples per segment and a once-per-delta field dies at T0'. Mutation: encode (incarnationId, flushSeq) ONCE per delta and fill every decoded SegmentCommit from that one copy. Measured against the three fixtures the sentence names:
- format/src/test/java/binjava/format/BatchedCommitDeltaTest.java:27-45 -- seg(key, id, partition, count, first) takes no pod and no flush parameter; the three segments differ ONLY in segmentKey ('bins/pod-a', 'bins/pod-b', 'bins/pod-c') and in RunKey/offsets. The minimal edit that satisfies 'different triples' is one fixture-wide incarnation constant with the pods left as they are: the three encoded PAIRS are then identical, the mutation round-trips, and assertThat(decoded).isEqualTo(original) at :52 passes.
- sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/BatchingSequencerTest.java:259 -- commitAll(List.of(from("pod0", 0), from("pod1", 0))). BOTH requests already carry flushSeq 0; the only thing distinguishing them is podId, the field just dropped from the payload. Add one shared incarnation to from(String, long) and both pairs are (INC, 0); the mutation passes hasSize(2) and every other assertion in that test.
- format/src/test/resources/golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin -- see the minor below; it cannot carry the field at all.
Under the PREVIOUS full-triple payload these fixtures discriminated BY CONSTRUCTION, because podId varied. The narrowing removed that, and the sentence that was true before it is false after it.

REMEDY, and per the packet's own advice deletion is preferable to another rewrite: either delete the shape prescription and the fixture sentence from backlog-notes.md entirely (backlog.md:123 and ADR:97-101 already state the shape correctly and agree with each other), or make both sentences say PAIR and say the fixtures must differ in `incarnationId` or `flushSeq` -- differing pods is no longer enough. Fixing notes:250 alone does not fix :254; fixing :254 alone leaves ADR:111 wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: A session implements M4.10c from backlog-notes.md#m410c: it adds podId back onto SegmentCommit (notes:250 says 'the triple'), and satisfies 'DIFFERENT triples per segment' by leaving the fixtures' existing pods as the varying field with one shared incarnation constant. It then writes the once-per-delta encoder -- one (incarnationId, flushSeq) for the whole delta, copied onto every decoded SegmentCommit -- and BatchedCommitDeltaTest, BatchingSequencerTest and the goldens are all GREEN, because every pair in every fixture is identical. The delta ships to M5's first forwarded multi-pod batch and drops every pod but one, which is the exact failure this ADR spent six rounds pinning.

findings.title: One of the three named discriminating fixtures is a committed golden that the same ADR requires to stay untouched
findings.detail: ADR:108-112 and notes:252-254 name `golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin` among the fixtures to be 'given DIFFERENT triples per segment', while ADR:117-119 requires 'Existing goldens are untouched and new ones added beside them (M3.0)'. GoldenChainEntryTest.java:69-84 decodes that file and asserts delta.encode() is BYTE-IDENTICAL to it, so the file cannot gain a per-segment field: it can only pin backward compatibility. A session following the sentence literally regenerates a committed golden, which converts a compat pin into a tautology that round-trips whatever was just written -- the shape non-negotiable 2 forbids. The discriminating golden has to be a NEW file beside it. One clause fixes it, or it goes with the deleted sentence in the major above.
findings.failure_scenario: A session gives golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin the new per-segment field by regenerating it. GoldenChainEntryTest.aBatchedDeltaFromAnEarlierBuildStillParses then round-trips bytes the current build just wrote, so it passes for any encoder change whatsoever: the one test that would have caught 'old objects stopped decoding' now asserts nothing about the old format, and a v1 delta sitting in a real bucket becomes undecodable with no test failing.

findings.title: The 'budget for rewritten assertions' paragraph names the Math::max test but not the version-refusal test the tolerance requirement collides with
findings.detail: notes:281-284 name the `Math::max`-over-bare-podId test (verified: CheckpointWriter.java:126-129, comment intact and its premise does invert -- an incarnation-blind max leaves the slot at (I2, 5) after a restart's first commit, so the SECOND commit at (I2, 1) is refused and a depth-one discriminator passes). Not named: format/src/test/java/binjava/format/CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest.java:112-121, anUNKNOWNVersionSTOPSRatherThanGuessingTheLayout, which does `bytes[7] = 1` on a freshly encoded fixture and asserts 'unsupported checkpoint version'. Once M4.10c bumps Checkpoint.VERSION to 1 that byte edit is a NO-OP and the fixture decodes cleanly. It fails LOUDLY rather than silently, which is why this is minor and not major -- but the ADR's version-TOLERANT requirement (ADR:132-137) points straight at that guard, and the guard's own comment records that deleting the version check left the whole build green. Tolerance must accept an ENUMERATED older version, never any version; otherwise this is an existing assertion weakened alongside a production change, which is what check-test-integrity.sh exists for. The M3.0 citation already in notes:277-280 ('accepts BOTH versions') implies the right shape, so this is a pointer, not a contradiction.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10c bumps Checkpoint.VERSION to 1 and makes decode tolerant. CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest's bytes[7]=1 is now a no-op, the test fails, and the quickest green is to relax the guard to accept any version rather than to move the constant to 2. A future v2 checkpoint written by a newer node is then decoded with the v1 layout by an old node instead of being refused -- silent misparse of a durable object, with the guard's own comment ('deleting the version check left the whole build green') recording that nothing else holds it.

findings.title: Pod attribution from the tail is sound but needs a segment-key accessor no row owns, and every fixture key the ADR names is unparseable
findings.detail: Checked, because the omission of podId rests entirely on it: the claim is TRUE of production -- DefaultIngest.java:349 passes podShortId as CommitRequest.podId and published.key() as segmentKey, and SegmentPublisher.java:133 builds that key from the same podShortId, so the two values agree by construction. Extraction is also well-DEFINED: SegmentKey's constructor bans '-' and '/' in podShortId (SegmentKey.java:80-83), which is exactly what makes the field unambiguous inside the rendered tail. What does not exist is any way to read it: SegmentKey exposes only headerLenOf(String), there is no parse/podShortIdOf, and SegmentCommit.java:27-32 validates segmentKey only as non-empty, so nothing forces it to be a rendered key at all. Every segmentKey in the fixtures this ADR names is NOT one -- 'bins/a.seg', 'bins/pod-a/0000000000000001.bseg', 'bins/pod' + n + '/0.bseg' -- and headerLenOf throws 'not a segment key' on all of them. So an M4.10d test that rebuilds the pod window from the uncheckpointed tail needs an accessor neither M4.10c nor M4.10d names, plus fixture keys rendered through SegmentKey. It fails loudly at implementation time rather than producing a green-but-empty test, so minor -- but it is unowned scope sitting between c and d, and one clause in the M4.10c row would place it.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.10d writes 'a successor rebuilds the pod window from the uncheckpointed tail'. There is no accessor for podShortId on a rendered key, so the session either adds an ad-hoc substring parse inside the sequencer (no test, no grammar guard, and SegmentCommit accepts any non-empty string) or, finding every fixture key unparseable, quietly narrows the test to a single pod -- at which point the window rebuild is exercised without ever attributing two segments to two different pods, and a rebuild that assigns every tail segment to one podId passes.

verified_this_round: Staged bytes hash to 374740d7 and the diff is docs-only: 7 files, no .java staged (git diff --cached --stat). The earlier code-file staging in the session snapshot is not in this commit.

ROUND-6 MAJOR FIXED: backlog.md:123 no longer claims 'only M5 tells them apart' and no longer says the placements are invisible to tests; it now states the shape and the minting site. Confirmed against the staged file, not the diff.

ROUND-6 MINOR FIXED: SPEC.md T0 row now reads 'and one keyed on the bare (podId, flushSeq), which dedups a retry within an incarnation but SUPPRESSES a restarted pod's new commit' -- the mutation and its direction, both named.

PARENT QUESTION 2, ANSWERED YES. IngestCommitPathTest.java:127-152 Recording implements Sequencer and records at commitAll (the seam primitive), decorating the real leased sequencer. The test at :80-98 already constructs DefaultIngest directly with an explicit podShortId 'pod7' and already observes TWO flushes from ONE instance with flushSeq 0 then 1. So 'one instance's two flushes record the SAME incarnation' kills the per-flush mutation (UUID.randomUUID() beside flushSeq++ in flushLocked, DefaultIngest.java:349), and 'two instances sharing a podShortId record DIFFERENT incarnations' kills a static or shared id. Both instances are constructible today, sequentially, each with its own TestSequencers.leased sequencer (IngestTestSupport.java:89-91); no fencing problem because the first is closed first. ONE CAVEAT WORTH A SENTENCE IN THE ROW: two instances sharing a podShortId over one store is exactly the M4.46 collision shape, so the assertion must be on the recorded CommitRequests, never on what is in the store.

PARENT QUESTION 1, ANSWERED IN PRINCIPLE YES / IN PRACTICE NO. A per-segment PAIR still kills once-per-delta, and binding the pair to the segment KEY (not to list position) still kills a request/segment swap -- the narrowing does not weaken either in principle. It does remove the field that made all three named fixtures discriminating by construction, and the guidance was not updated with it: see the major.

SegmentCommit's javadoc really does cite the two-attributions hazard the ADR credits it with ('nothing in that shape would stop two runs of the same segment naming different keys', SegmentCommit.java:20-23).
CheckpointTest.java:153-169: the 64 KiB assertion and the ~38 KiB 1,600-stream comment are both there, as quoted.
Checkpoint.java:151 is a strict version equality; CheckpointCursor.java:67 does define IOException as 'the store is unreachable'. ADR:132-137 accurate.

DefaultIngest.java:349 evaluates flushSeq++ inside the CommitRequest argument, so the counter advances even when commit throws -- the M4.10d note's 'unconditional flushSeq++ on a commit that then threw' and 'density is over ISSUED flushes' are both correct, and this is the claim that makes a blanket refuse-then-re-flush unsafe.
SPEC.md :55, :501 and :511 in the STAGED file do each carry '(podId, flushSeq, ...)' as descriptive seam text. Line citations are correct post-diff, not stale.
CommitRequest is not encoded anywhere -- CheckpointWriter.capture reads podId/flushSeq off it and encodes into Checkpoint -- so 'it is never encoded, so it is not one of the two FORMATS' holds.
GoldenChainEntryTest.java:74-80: the batched golden does carry two distinct segments, asserted with containsExactly over SegmentCommit records, plus byte-identical re-encode.
